note: Backcountry ski areas across Canada, shown in Skiing (ski-areas.js). Hand-edited. Text is written for Trail Finder from the linked official and local sources (park agencies, avalanche centres, hut owners); open each link for the full, current rules. ates = officially published Avalanche Terrain Exposure Scale ratings for named trips in the area, copied by name with the class (1 Simple, 2 Challenging, 3 Complex) from atesSrc; Parks Canada's list is dated 2017-04-05; Kananaskis ratings are the examples Alberta Parks names on its ATES page (its full ratings are on its interactive map). forecast: who publishes the avalanche forecast here (ac Avalanche Canada, pc Parks Canada, kc Kananaskis Country, aq Avalanche Quebec, none = no public forecast); sub = the Avalanche Canada subregion when known. approx = spot is approximate. Checked 2026-10-24.

pc.name: Parks Canada, Avalanche Terrain Ratings for backcountry touring in the Mountain National Parks (2017)

kc.name: Alberta Parks, Kananaskis Country Avalanche Terrain Ratings (ATES)

areas.name: Mount Seymour backcountry
areas.about: Vancouver's closest touring: Brockton Point, Pump Peak, Tim Jones Peak and Mount Seymour's summit past the ski area. Short days, but steep rolls and cliffy gullies (Elsay Lake side) catch people every year.
areas.access: Park at the top of Mount Seymour Road (ski area lots) and go up the Mount Seymour Trail along the ski area's edge.
areas.rules: Mount Seymour Provincial Park: free, no permit. Uphill only on the park trail, not on the runs.

areas.name: Cypress, Hollyburn and Black Mountain
areas.about: Mount Strachan, Black Mountain and Hollyburn Peak around Cypress Mountain: short tours with views of the city, deep coastal snow and steep gullies on Strachan's north side.
areas.access: Cypress Bowl Road to the ski area lots; follow Cypress's uphill and backcountry access routes.
areas.rules: Cypress Provincial Park. Check Cypress Mountain's uphill rules before skinning on the ski area.

areas.name: Sky Pilot and Sea to Sky Gondola backcountry
areas.about: From the top of the Sea to Sky Gondola: Sky Pilot Valley, Mount Habrich and the Sky Pilot group. Big alpine terrain an hour from Vancouver.
areas.access: Ride the Sea to Sky Gondola in Squamish (ticket) and follow its backcountry access route past the marked boundary.
areas.rules: Follow the gondola's backcountry rules (some days the access closes). Beyond the boundary there is no patrol.

areas.name: Elfin Lakes and Diamond Head
areas.about: The classic first overnight tour: 11 km up Paul Ridge to the Elfin Lakes Shelter, then the Gargoyles, Columnar Peak and Mamquam Lake. Mostly gentle, with real avalanche slopes off the ridge.
areas.access: Diamond Head trailhead at the end of the Mamquam (Garibaldi Park) road from Squamish; winter tires or chains, the last part can need 4x4.

huts.name: Elfin Lakes Shelter
huts.note: BC Parks, reservation and fee for nights

areas.rules: Garibaldi Provincial Park: book the shelter or camping before you go; no snowmobiles in the park.

areas.name: Garibaldi Névé Traverse
areas.about: Three days on glaciers from Elfin Lakes over the Garibaldi Névé, past Mount Garibaldi and the Sharkfin, down to Garibaldi Lake. Crevasses and whiteouts: glacier skills needed.
areas.access: Start at the Diamond Head trailhead (Elfin Lakes), finish at the Rubble Creek trailhead; arrange a car at each end.
areas.rules: Garibaldi Provincial Park: reserve the nights you'll spend in the park.

areas.name: Garibaldi Lake, Sphinx and Black Tusk
areas.about: Long climb up the Rubble Creek switchbacks to Garibaldi Lake, then the Sphinx and Sentinel glaciers, Panorama Ridge and the Black Tusk. Don't cross the lake unless it's well frozen.
areas.access: Rubble Creek trailhead off Highway 99 south of Whistler (Garibaldi Lake parking).
areas.rules: Garibaldi Provincial Park: reservation and fee to camp.

areas.name: Brohm Ridge
areas.about: Open alpine ridge below Mount Garibaldi's west side and the Warren Glacier, shared with snowmobiles.
areas.access: Brohm Ridge forest road north of Squamish; 4x4 and chains, often reached by sled.
areas.rules: Shared with motorized users; part of the ridge is a snowmobile club area.

areas.name: Tantalus Range and Lake Lovely Water
areas.about: Steep, glaciated peaks across the Squamish River (Alpha, Serratus, Tantalus). Remote and serious in winter.
areas.access: Cross the Squamish River by boat, then a very steep trail; or fly in by helicopter.

huts.name: Lake Lovely Water hut
huts.by: Alpine Club of Canada, Vancouver section

areas.rules: Tantalus Provincial Park.

areas.name: Callaghan Valley
areas.about: Rolling alpine terrain around Callaghan Lake, Mount Callaghan and the Solitude Glacier, plus the lodge-based touring of Callaghan Country.
areas.access: Callaghan Valley Road (Whistler Olympic Park turn-off) off Highway 99; beyond the plowed road you ski or sled in.
areas.rules: Callaghan Lake Provincial Park. Callaghan Country trails need their trail pass.

areas.name: Brandywine Meadows
areas.about: Big open meadows and bowls below Brandywine Mountain, popular with skiers and sledders.
areas.access: Brandywine forest road off Highway 99 between Squamish and Whistler; 4x4, or ski/sled the road.
areas.rules: Shared with snowmobiles.

areas.name: Musical Bumps, Singing Pass and Russet Lake
areas.about: From Whistler Peak over Piccolo, Flute and Oboe to Russet Lake, with tours to Fissile, Castle Towers and the Overlord Glacier. The Singing Pass valley is threaded by avalanche paths.
areas.access: Whistler Mountain lifts (backcountry/uphill ticket) to Whistler Peak, or skin the Singing Pass trail from Whistler Village (long).

huts.name: Kees and Claire Hut
huts.note: at Russet Lake, booking and fee

areas.rules: Garibaldi Provincial Park beyond the ski area boundary.

areas.name: Spearhead Traverse
areas.about: Canada's best-known one- or two-day ski traverse: about 34 km and 13 glaciers in a horseshoe from Blackcomb to Whistler. Crevasses, cornices and big exposure.
areas.access: Start from Blackcomb's Showcase T-bar or Blackcomb Glacier (lift ticket), finish down Whistler Mountain.
areas.rules: Garibaldi Provincial Park; ski area rules apply until you leave the boundary.

areas.name: Wedgemount Lake and Wedge Mountain
areas.about: A steep 1,200 m climb to a glacier lake under Wedge Mountain, the highest peak in Garibaldi Park; spring couloirs and the Armchair Glacier.
areas.access: Wedgemount trailhead off Highway 99 north of Whistler (Wedge Creek road).

huts.name: Wedgemount Lake hut
huts.note: small hut at the lake; check BC Parks

areas.rules: Garibaldi Provincial Park: reserve to camp.

areas.name: Rainbow and Sproatt
areas.about: Whistler's west-side touring: Sproatt's alpine bowls and Rainbow Mountain, both right above the valley.
areas.access: Alta Lake Road side of Whistler (Rainbow trailhead, or the Sproatt trails from Alta Vista).
areas.rules: Rainbow Lake is Whistler's water supply (21 Mile Creek watershed): no camping and no dogs there.

areas.name: Joffre Lakes and Matier Glacier
areas.about: Steep glaciated peaks above the Joffre Lakes: Matier, Joffre, Slalok, the Twin Couloirs and Tszil. One of the Duffey's busiest zones.
areas.access: Joffre Lakes parking on Highway 99 (Duffey Lake Road) east of Pemberton.
areas.rules: Joffre Lakes Provincial Park (Pipi7íyekw); check BC Parks for passes and closures.

areas.name: Duffey Lake Road peaks
areas.about: Roadside alpine touring off Highway 99: Mount Rohr, Cayoosh, Chief Pascall, Vantage, Mount Brew. Drier inland snow than Whistler, often with buried weak layers.
areas.access: Pull-outs along Highway 99 between Joffre Lakes and Duffey Lake; Cayoosh Pass is the high point.
areas.rules: Park well off the highway; the road is plowed but not always open.

areas.name: Marriott Basin
areas.about: A sheltered basin of rolling alpine terrain north of the Duffey: Mount Marriott, Mount Rohr's north side and Cerise Creek's neighbours.
areas.access: From the Cayoosh Creek side of Highway 99, about 3 hours of skinning.

huts.name: Wendy Thompson Hut
huts.by: Alpine Club of Canada, Whistler section

areas.name: Cerise Creek and Keith's Hut
areas.about: Below the Anniversary Glacier and Mount Matier's east side: tree skiing, the Vantage col and Joffre's north side.
areas.access: Highway 99, Cerise Creek pull-out east of Joffre Lakes.

huts.name: Keith's Hut
huts.note: first come, first served; often full

areas.name: Tenquille Lake
areas.about: An alpine lake and cabin north of Pemberton with open ridges all around. Long winter approach, often by sled.
areas.access: Hurley forest road or the Tenquille Lake trail from the Birkenhead side; usually sled-assisted in winter.

huts.name: Tenquille Lake cabin
huts.note: public cabin, first come, first served

areas.name: Coquihalla Summit
areas.about: Roadside touring off Highway 5: Zupjok, Needle Peak, Yak, Thar and Zoa. Short days with steep faces; storms bring a lot of snow fast.
areas.access: Zopkios rest area (brake check) and the Falls Lake exit on the Coquihalla Highway.
areas.rules: Highway avalanche control: never ski slopes that run onto the highway, and obey closures when control work is on.

areas.name: Manning Park backcountry
areas.about: The Three Brothers, Blackwall Peak and the Heather Trail ridges above Manning Park Resort; gentler terrain than the coast.
areas.access: Manning Park Resort (Gibson Pass) or the lodge on Highway 3.
areas.rules: E.C. Manning Provincial Park.

areas.name: Tetrahedron Park
areas.about: Gentle subalpine touring and a hut-to-hut network on the Sunshine Coast, with Tetrahedron Peak and Mount Steele above.
areas.access: Ferry to Langdale, then the Gray Creek / Tetrahedron forest roads from Sechelt (4x4 or ski the road).

huts.name: Edwards, Bachelor, Mount Steele and McNair cabins
huts.by: Tetrahedron Outdoor Club with BC Parks

areas.rules: Tetrahedron Provincial Park, part of Chapman Creek watershed: no camping outside the cabins.

areas.name: Knuckleheads
areas.about: Powell River's winter recreation area: open ridges, a cabin and treed slopes.
areas.access: Branch roads from Powell River; 4x4 or sled.

areas.name: Forbidden Plateau and Mount Albert Edward
areas.about: From Mount Washington into Strathcona Park: rolling plateau, Mount Albert Edward and Castlecrag. Weather moves in fast off the ocean.
areas.access: Paradise Meadows trailhead (Raven Lodge) at Mount Washington.
areas.rules: Strathcona Provincial Park. Stay off the groomed nordic trails unless you have a nordic pass.

areas.name: Mount Cain backcountry
areas.about: A small community ski hill on north Vancouver Island with easy access to steep bowls and couloirs around it.
areas.access: Mount Cain ski area road off Highway 19 (open on ski days).

areas.name: 5040 Peak and Cobalt Lake
areas.about: Alpine bowls above Cobalt Lake near Port Alberni, with a hut and views to the ocean.
areas.access: Marion Creek forest road off Highway 4.

huts.name: 5040 Peak hut
huts.by: Alpine Club of Canada, Vancouver Island section

areas.name: Mount Arrowsmith
areas.about: Gullies and open slopes on the old Mount Arrowsmith ski area and Cokely, above Port Alberni.
areas.access: Cameron Main / Pass Main logging roads from Highway 4; 4x4.

areas.name: Kootenay Pass
areas.about: Highway 3's summit at 1,775 m: Ripple Ridge, Cornice Ridge and Lightning Strike, all close to the road. One of BC's most popular roadside tours.
areas.access: Summit parking at Bridal Lake (Stagleap Provincial Park) on Highway 3 between Salmo and Creston.
areas.rules: Highway avalanche control: never ski slopes that run onto the highway, and obey closures when control work is on. Some slopes above the highway are closed to skiing.

areas.name: Whitewater and Ymir backcountry
areas.about: Light, deep Kootenay snow around Whitewater ski area: Ymir Peak, Evening Ridge, the Hummingbird and Five Mile basins.
areas.access: Whitewater ski area road from Highway 6 near Nelson; backcountry access through the ski area's gates and uphill routes.
areas.rules: Follow Whitewater's uphill policy. Commercial cat and lodge tenures nearby (Ymir backcountry lodges).

areas.name: Kokanee Glacier Park
areas.about: High alpine bowls around Kokanee Glacier, with a big hut. Mostly reached by helicopter for week-long stays.
areas.access: Winter access is mainly by helicopter; skiing in from Gibson Lake is long and serious.

huts.name: Kokanee Glacier Cabin
huts.by: Alpine Club of Canada with BC Parks

areas.rules: Kokanee Glacier Provincial Park.

areas.name: Bonnington Range Traverse
areas.about: A multi-day hut-to-hut traverse between Nelson and Castlegar over rolling subalpine ridges.
areas.access: Usually from Bombi Summit (Highway 3) or the Erie Creek side; leave a car at the other end.

huts.name: Grassy, Steed, Copper and Huckleberry cabins
huts.note: public cabins along the way; check their state before you go

areas.name: Rossland Range
areas.about: Old Glory, Mount Plewman and the ridges north of Rossland, with a network of small day and overnight cabins.
areas.access: Nancy Greene Summit and other pull-outs on Highway 3B north of Rossland.

areas.name: Valhalla Range
areas.about: Granite peaks and glaciers west of Slocan Lake, mostly skied from lodges.
areas.access: Logging roads from the Slocan Valley; lodges fly or sled their guests in.

huts.name: Valhalla Mountain Touring and other lodges

areas.rules: Valhalla Provincial Park.

areas.name: Fernie and the Lizard Range
areas.about: The Lizard Range's huge snowfall: bowls and chutes beyond Fernie Alpine Resort and around Island Lake.
areas.access: Fernie Alpine Resort's backcountry gates, or the Island Lake and Hosmer roads.
areas.rules: Island Lake Lodge's cat-skiing tenure is next to the resort: respect its boundaries.

areas.name: Castle Mountain and Castle Wildland
areas.about: Steep ridges and chutes beyond Castle Mountain Resort in the Castle Provincial and Wildland Parks; also Crowsnest Pass tours nearby.
areas.access: Castle Mountain Resort (Highway 774 west of Pincher Creek).

areas.name: Jumbo Pass
areas.about: Purcell Mountains alpine above the Jumbo Valley, west of Invermere, with a hut at the pass.
areas.access: Jumbo Creek forest road from Invermere / Panorama, mostly sled-assisted in winter.

areas.name: Bugaboos
areas.about: Granite spires and big glaciers. Spring ski mountaineering and the start of the Bugaboos to Rogers Pass traverse.
areas.access: The Bugaboo road isn't plowed in winter: a long ski or sled from Brisco; the area is also heli-skiing tenure.

huts.name: Conrad Kain Hut
huts.by: Alpine Club of Canada with BC Parks

areas.rules: Bugaboo Provincial Park.

areas.name: Kicking Horse backcountry
areas.about: Terminator, Ozone and the Dogtooth Range from the top of Kicking Horse resort.
areas.access: Kicking Horse Mountain Resort's backcountry gates (Golden).

areas.name: Esplanade Range lodges
areas.about: Hut-to-hut touring in the northern Selkirks north of Golden, between privately run lodges.
areas.access: Helicopter from Golden.

areas.name: Mount Mackenzie and Mount Cartier
areas.about: Big Selkirks terrain right above Revelstoke: Mount Cartier from town and the backcountry past Revelstoke Mountain Resort.
areas.access: Revelstoke Mountain Resort's backcountry gates, or the Mount Cartier trail/road south of town.
areas.rules: Commercial heli and cat tenures surround Revelstoke.

areas.name: Mount Revelstoke National Park
areas.about: Subalpine meadows and the Clachnacudainn Range above Revelstoke. The Meadows in the Sky Parkway is closed in winter, so you ski or snowshoe up it.
areas.access: Meadows in the Sky Parkway gate, just north of Revelstoke on Highway 1.
ates: Meadows in the Sky Parkway Summit Trail to 8 Mile Crossing
Balsam Lake to Eva & Miller Lakes
Balsam Lake to Mt Revelstoke Summit
areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit).

links.t: Parks Canada: Mount Revelstoke National Park

areas.name: Rogers Pass (Glacier National Park)
areas.about: Canada's most famous touring centre: the Asulkan, Illecillewaet, Connaught and Bostock areas right off Highway 1. Huge avalanche paths over the highway.
areas.access: Highway 1 pull-outs and the Illecillewaet / Asulkan lot near the Rogers Pass Discovery Centre.

huts.name: Wheeler Hut, Asulkan Cabin, Glacier Circle Cabin

areas.rules: Winter permit system: you need a Parks Canada winter permit and must check each day which areas are open; entering a closed area is illegal because of highway and railway avalanche control.
ates: Rogers Pass Ski Hill (forest cuts behind hotel)

areas.name: Fairy Meadow (Adamant Range)
areas.about: A legendary hut in the Adamant Range of the northern Selkirks: glaciers, deep snow and week-long stays.
areas.access: Helicopter from the Golden or Blaeberry side for week-long bookings.

areas.name: Trophy Mountain (Wells Gray)
areas.about: Open meadows and rolling alpine terrain on the edge of Wells Gray Park, near Clearwater.
areas.access: Trophy Mountain road from Highway 5 north of Clearwater; sled-assisted when the road isn't plowed.
areas.rules: Wells Gray Provincial Park.

areas.name: Pine Pass
areas.about: Highway 97's pass through the northern Rockies near Powder King: deep snow, short approaches and few people.
areas.access: Pull-outs on Highway 97 at Pine Pass and the Azouzetta Lake area.
areas.rules: Highway avalanche control: never ski slopes that run onto the highway, and obey closures when control work is on.

areas.name: Hudson Bay Mountain
areas.about: Glacier and bowls above Ski Smithers, plus the Prairie and Harvey Mountain tours nearby.
areas.access: Ski Smithers road; backcountry beyond the ski area boundary.

areas.name: Babine Mountains
areas.about: Big, rolling alpine terrain north of Smithers with several public cabins.
areas.access: Driftwood or Harvey Mountain roads from Smithers; sled-shared areas have set routes.

huts.name: Public cabins (Joe L'Orsa Cabin in Silver King Basin and others)

areas.rules: Babine Mountains Provincial Park: snowmobiles only in set areas.

areas.name: Shames Mountain backcountry
areas.about: Deep coastal snow next to the community co-op ski hill west of Terrace: bowls, glades and the Shames backcountry touring area.
areas.access: Shames Mountain road off Highway 16; sign out through the ski area's backcountry access.

areas.name: Bear Pass (Stewart)
areas.about: Huge glaciated terrain along Highway 37A near Stewart, one of the snowiest roads in North America. Heli-skiing tenure all around.
areas.access: Pull-outs on Highway 37A between Meziadin Junction and Stewart.
areas.rules: Highway avalanche control: never ski slopes that run onto the highway, and obey closures when control work is on.

areas.name: Haines Pass (Chilkat Pass)
areas.about: Treeless alpine terrain along the Haines Highway in the far northwest corner of BC, between Haines Junction (Yukon) and Haines (Alaska).
areas.access: Pull-outs on Highway 3 (Haines Road); border crossings at Dalton Cache on the Alaska side.
areas.rules: Bring a passport if you'll cross the Alaska border.

areas.name: White Pass and Fraser
areas.about: The Yukon's main ski touring area, around the Klondike Highway on the BC side of the Alaska border: wind-blown alpine terrain, from mellow to big lines.
areas.access: Pull-outs along Highway 2 between Log Cabin and the border; the Canadian customs post is at Fraser.
areas.rules: Slopes on the US side need you to clear customs; ski with a passport.

areas.name: Wheaton Valley and Mount Skukum
areas.about: Alpine bowls south of Whitehorse along the Annie Lake road, forecasted together with White Pass.
areas.access: Annie Lake / Wheaton River road from the South Klondike Highway.

areas.name: Montana Mountain (Carcross)
areas.about: The big mountain above Carcross, with old mining roads leading into the alpine.
areas.access: Montana Mountain road from Carcross.

areas.name: Tombstone Territorial Park
areas.about: Spring touring among granite peaks off the Dempster Highway, under almost endless daylight in April.
areas.access: Dempster Highway, about 70 km north of the Klondike Highway junction (near Dawson City).
areas.rules: Remote, no cell service; no public avalanche forecast.

areas.name: Kluane icefields
areas.about: The largest non-polar icefields on Earth, under Mount Logan and the Saint Elias Range. Expedition ski mountaineering.
areas.access: Ski plane from the Haines Junction area.
areas.rules: Parks Canada requires registration for icefield trips; no public avalanche forecast.

areas.name: King's Throne (Kluane front ranges)
areas.about: A big cirque above Kathleen Lake, the classic spring ski in Kluane's front ranges.
areas.access: Kathleen Lake day-use area on the Haines Road, south of Haines Junction.
areas.rules: Kluane National Park; no public avalanche forecast.

areas.name: Wapta Icefield and huts
areas.about: The Rockies' classic hut-to-hut glacier traverse between Peyto Lake and the Yoho Valley, with peaks like Mount Gordon, Olive and Rhondda from the huts.
areas.access: Bow Lake (Num-Ti-Jah lot) or Peyto Lake on the Icefields Parkway; exit via the Yoho Valley or Sherbrooke Lake to Highway 1.

huts.name: Bow Hut, Peyto Hut, Balfour Hut, Scott Duncan Hut

areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit). Crevasses and whiteouts: glacier skills needed.
ates: Bow hut to Balfour hut via Nic/Olive col

areas.name: Bow Summit and Observation Peak
areas.about: The highest point of the Icefields Parkway: easy-to-reach alpine terrain, Observation Peak's subpeaks and the slopes above Peyto Lake.
areas.access: Bow Summit (Peyto Lake) lot, or pull-outs on the Icefields Parkway.

areas.name: Helen Lake, Cirque Peak and Dolomite
areas.about: Popular tours across the Parkway from Crowfoot: the Katherine and Helen Lakes circuit, Cirque Peak and the long Dolomite Peak circuit.
areas.access: Helen Lake trailhead, across the Icefields Parkway from the Crowfoot Glacier viewpoint.

areas.name: Crowfoot Glades and Crowfoot Pass
areas.about: Tree skiing and a pass climb on Crowfoot Mountain's north side, right above Bow Lake.
areas.access: Pull-outs on the Icefields Parkway near Bow Lake.

areas.name: Mosquito Creek and Mount Hector
areas.about: Valley touring up Mosquito Creek to Molar Pass and North Molar, and Mount Hector's big glaciated ascent nearby.
areas.access: Mosquito Creek on the Icefields Parkway (hostel and lot); Mount Hector from the Parkway pull-out near Hector Lake.

areas.name: Parker Ridge and Hilda
areas.about: Short climbs to big views over the Saskatchewan Glacier at the north end of Banff park: Parker Ridge, Hilda Ridge, and longer days to the Castleguard.
areas.access: Parker Ridge lot and Hilda Creek on the Icefields Parkway, south of the Columbia Icefield.

areas.name: Columbia Icefield
areas.about: The Rockies' biggest icefield: Athabasca Glacier, Snow Dome, Mount Columbia, the Twins and Kitchener. Ski mountaineering with icefalls and crevasses.
areas.access: Athabasca Glacier toe lot off the Icefields Parkway; Wilcox Pass trailhead nearby.
areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit). No huts on the icefield: you camp.

areas.name: Skoki and the Lake Louise backcountry
areas.about: Behind the Lake Louise ski area: Boulder and Deception passes to historic Skoki Lodge, Fossil Mountain, Merlin Valley and the Hidden Bowl.
areas.access: Fish Creek parking at the Lake Louise ski area; ski the Temple road and up past the ski area.
ates: Lake Louise resort backcountry accessed from ski area
areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit).

areas.name: Lake Louise, Paradise Valley and Moraine Lake road
areas.about: Tours from Lake Louise: the Moraine Lake road (closed to cars in winter), Paradise Valley, Mount Fairview and the Plain of Six Glaciers, whose trail crosses big avalanche paths.
areas.access: Lake Louise lakeshore and the Moraine Lake road gate.

areas.name: Sunshine Village and Healy Pass
areas.about: High meadows around Sunshine Village: Healy Pass, the Monarch ramparts and the slopes past the ski area boundary.
areas.access: Sunshine Village parking (Healy Creek trail), or the ski area's backcountry exits.
ates: Healy Creek - Sundance to SSV road
Healy Creek – SSV to Healy Pass
Sunshine Village backcountry accessed from ski area

areas.name: Egypt Lake and Shadow Lake
areas.about: Overnight tours into the Egypt Lake basin (shelter) or Shadow Lake (lodge) under the Great Divide, with Haiduk Lake and Gibbon Pass between.
areas.access: Redearth Creek trailhead on Highway 1, or over Healy Pass from Sunshine.
areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit).

areas.name: Mount Assiniboine
areas.about: The 'Matterhorn of the Rockies': rolling meadows and bowls around Lake Magog, with a historic lodge and public cabins.
areas.access: A long ski in from Mount Shark (Spray Lakes, Kananaskis) via Bryant Creek and Assiniboine Pass, or from Sunshine; or a helicopter from Mount Shark on set days.
areas.rules: Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park (BC); the approach crosses Banff National Park (wilderness pass to camp there).

areas.name: Banff and Bow Valley tours
areas.about: Low-angle valley tours and big ascents near Banff and Castle Junction: Johnston Creek, Taylor Lake, Boom Lake, Castle Mountain and Mystic Pass.
areas.access: Trailheads along Highway 1 and the Bow Valley Parkway.

areas.name: Vermilion Pass, Stanley Glacier and Chickadee
areas.about: Steep terrain off Highway 93 South: Stanley Glacier's headwall, Storm Mountain, Chickadee Valley and Tokumm Creek. Quick access, serious slopes.
areas.access: Stanley Glacier and Chickadee Valley trailheads on Highway 93 South, just west of the Alberta border.

areas.name: Little Yoho Valley
areas.about: Big alpine bowls and peaks around the Stanley Mitchell Hut: President Pass, Kiwetinok Pass, Mount McArthur and Isolated Col. Has its own Parks Canada forecast.
areas.access: Ski the Yoho Valley Road (closed to cars in winter) from Highway 1 near Field, then up past Takakkaw Falls: a long first day.
areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit).

areas.name: Lake O'Hara
areas.about: 11 km up the closed Lake O'Hara road to a hut among some of the Rockies' finest peaks: Opabin and Odaray plateaus, Schaefer Basin, McArthur Pass.
areas.access: Lake O'Hara parking at Highway 1 (west of Kicking Horse Pass); ski the road.
ates: Lake O'Hara Road to Elizabeth Parker Hut
Lake O'Hara Circuit (avoid the north shoreline)
areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit).

areas.name: Emerald Lake and Field
areas.about: Gentle nordic trails at Emerald Lake and big avalanche terrain right above it (Emerald Pass, the Emerald Peak slide path), plus Mount Field and Sherbrooke Lake.
areas.access: Emerald Lake road from Field, and the Sherbrooke Lake lot at West Louise Lodge on Highway 1.
ates: Field to Emerald Lake Nordic trail

areas.name: Tonquin Valley
areas.about: Amethyst Lakes below the Ramparts, with the Wates-Gibson Hut and Fraser Glacier.
areas.access: Astoria River (Edith Cavell road, closed to cars in winter) or Portal Creek (Marmot Basin road).
areas.rules: Caribou range: Parks Canada closes the Tonquin Valley to winter travel for much of the season (recently Nov 1 to May 15). Check Jasper's closures before planning.

areas.name: Maligne Lake and the Bald Hills
areas.about: Open, rolling slopes of the Bald Hills above Maligne Lake, Little Shovel Pass and the Skyline.
areas.access: Maligne Lake at the end of the Maligne Lake Road from Jasper.
ates: Bald Hills Lookout Trail – to hitching rail only
areas.rules: Jasper has had delayed winter access in caribou ranges; check current closures.

areas.name: Marmot Basin backcountry and Whistlers Creek
areas.about: Bowls past Marmot Basin's boundary and Whistlers Creek, south of Jasper.
areas.access: Marmot Basin ski area road off Highway 93A.
ates: Marmot Basin backcountry accessed from ski area

areas.name: Fryatt Valley
areas.about: A long valley approach to a hut under Mount Fryatt, with alpine bowls above the headwall.
areas.access: Geraldine Lakes road from Highway 93A near Athabasca Falls, then the Fryatt Valley trail (long).
areas.rules: Overnight in the park needs a Parks Canada wilderness pass (backcountry permit).

areas.name: Waterton Lakes
areas.about: Where the prairies meet the mountains: Akamina Pass, Forum Lake and Ridge, Summit Lake, Rowe Lakes and Bertha Lake. Wild winds and wind slabs.
areas.access: Akamina Parkway toward Cameron Lake from Waterton townsite (check how far it's plowed).
ates: Cameron Lake trail to lake only

links.t: Parks Canada: Waterton Lakes National Park

areas.name: Burstall Pass and Robertson Glacier
areas.about: One of Kananaskis's most popular tours: flats past Burstall Lakes, then the pass, Snow Peak and the French, Haig and Robertson glaciers for the ski mountaineering traverse.
areas.access: Burstall Pass lot on the Smith-Dorrien / Spray Trail (Highway 742).
areas.rules: Park in Kananaskis only with a Kananaskis Conservation Pass.

links.t: Alberta Parks: Kananaskis avalanche terrain ratings (ATES map)

areas.name: Chester Lake and the Smith-Dorrien
areas.about: Chester Lake, Rummel Lake, Tryst Lake and Tent Ridge along the Smith-Dorrien: from gentle forest tours to the steep Tent Ridge horseshoe.
areas.access: Chester Lake, Rummel Lake and Mount Shark lots on the Smith-Dorrien / Spray Trail.
areas.rules: Park in Kananaskis only with a Kananaskis Conservation Pass.

links.t: Alberta Parks: Kananaskis avalanche terrain ratings (ATES map)

areas.name: Commonwealth Ridge and Black Prince
areas.about: Steep terrain near the Smith-Dorrien summit: Commonwealth Ridge, the Black Prince and Warspite bowls, Headwall Bowl, Purple Col.
areas.access: Commonwealth Creek, Black Prince and Headwall pull-outs on the Smith-Dorrien / Spray Trail.
areas.rules: Park in Kananaskis only with a Kananaskis Conservation Pass. Commonwealth Creek is a terrain trap.

links.t: Alberta Parks: Kananaskis avalanche terrain ratings (ATES map)

areas.name: Kananaskis Lakes, Elk Lakes and Aster Lake
areas.about: Valley tours from the Kananaskis Lakes: Elk Pass to the Elk Lakes cabin in BC, Aster Lake and the glaciers of Mount Joffre.
areas.access: Elk Pass and Upper Kananaskis Lake lots in Peter Lougheed Provincial Park.

huts.name: Elk Lakes Cabin
huts.note: in Elk Lakes Provincial Park (BC), booking

areas.rules: Park in Kananaskis only with a Kananaskis Conservation Pass.

links.t: Alberta Parks: Kananaskis avalanche terrain ratings (ATES map)

areas.name: Highwood Pass
areas.about: Canada's highest paved pass (2,206 m): Ptarmigan Cirque, Pocaterra Cirque and Mount Rae. Highway 40 is closed to cars over the pass from December 1 to mid-June, so it's a long ski in winter and a classic in June when the road opens.
areas.access: Winter gate at King Creek on Highway 40.
areas.rules: Park in Kananaskis only with a Kananaskis Conservation Pass.

links.t: Alberta Parks: Kananaskis avalanche terrain ratings (ATES map)

areas.name: Mont Ernest-Laforce
areas.about: A public backcountry sector in Parc national de la Gaspésie, with open bowls and glades down to the road. One of the most popular in the Chic-Chocs.
areas.access: Route 299 through the park; park at the sector's lot and skin up (about an hour).
areas.rules: Parc national de la Gaspésie: park access fee (Sépaq). Ski only in the authorized sectors; the rest of the park's summits protect the caribou.

links.t: Sépaq: Parc national de la Gaspésie

areas.name: Mont Albert authorized sectors
areas.about: Steep, snowy terrain on the Mont Albert massif. A large part of the mountain is closed to skiing to protect the endangered caribou: ski only in the authorized sectors.
areas.access: From the Gîte du Mont-Albert area on Route 299.
areas.rules: Parc national de la Gaspésie: access fee, authorized sectors only (caribou protection).

links.t: Sépaq: Parc national de la Gaspésie

areas.name: Mines Madeleine
areas.about: A sector in the Réserve faunique des Chic-Chocs with bowls and gullies near the old Madeleine mine.
areas.access: Route 299 / Mines Madeleine road; guided options too.
areas.rules: Réserve faunique des Chic-Chocs (Sépaq): check access rules and fees.

areas.name: Champ-de-Mars and Blanche-Lamontagne
areas.about: Big open slopes in the Chic-Chocs wildlife reserve, among the steepest public terrain in eastern Canada.
areas.access: Reserve roads off Route 299.
areas.rules: Réserve faunique des Chic-Chocs: access has been restricted after caribou sightings; check the current status with Sépaq.

areas.name: Mont Hog's Back
areas.about: A Chic-Chocs ridge with gullies and bowls on both sides, in the wildlife reserve.
areas.access: Off Route 299 in the Réserve faunique des Chic-Chocs.
areas.rules: Access has been restricted after caribou sightings; check with Sépaq before going.

areas.name: Mont Vallières-de-Saint-Réal
areas.about: A public sector of the Chic-Chocs wildlife reserve west of Mont Albert.
areas.access: Reserve roads off Route 299.
areas.rules: Réserve faunique des Chic-Chocs (Sépaq).

areas.name: Mont Lyall
areas.about: A 330 m vertical sector managed with the FQME, south of the park.
areas.access: Forest roads from Route 299 / Murdochville side.
areas.rules: FQME day or season membership (buy online) to ski here.

links.t: FQME (Quebec mountain federation): access and membership

areas.name: Marsoui
areas.about: A community-run sector with seaside access on the north coast of the Gaspé.
areas.access: From Route 132 in Marsoui.
areas.rules: FQME day or season membership.

links.t: FQME (Quebec mountain federation): access and membership

areas.name: Cap Castor
areas.about: A private backcountry domain with about 30 seaside runs east of Sainte-Anne-des-Monts, and a summit chalet.
areas.access: Route 132 east of Sainte-Anne-des-Monts.
areas.rules: Private: pay their access fee.

areas.name: Rivière-à-Claude valley (Coop RAC)
areas.about: Community-run backcountry sectors in the Rivière-à-Claude valley, with snowmobile shuttles and lodging.
areas.access: Route 132 at Rivière-à-Claude; snowmobile-assisted.
areas.rules: Run by the Coopérative de plein air RAC: book with them.

areas.name: Monts-Valin
areas.about: Deep, dry snow on the summits north of Saguenay (the 'Vallée des Fantômes' of snow-covered trees), with heated refuges. Mostly gentle terrain.
areas.access: Parc national des Monts-Valin entrance, north of Saint-Fulgence.
areas.rules: Sépaq park access fee; book the refuges.

areas.name: Traversée de Charlevoix
areas.about: A 100 km hut-to-hut backcountry ski traverse through the Charlevoix hills, with cabins and chalets each night.
areas.access: Starts near Saint-Urbain (Parc national des Grands-Jardins) and ends near Mont Grand-Fonds.

huts.name: Cabins and chalets along the route

areas.rules: Book with La Traversée de Charlevoix.

areas.name: Mont Hereford glades
areas.about: Glade (sous-bois) skiing on a community forest mountain near the US border, among the best in southern Quebec.
areas.access: Forêt Hereford parking areas near East Hereford / Saint-Herménégilde.
areas.rules: Community forest: follow their access rules and fees.

areas.name: Gros Morne: Long Range Mountains
areas.about: The highlands of the Long Range above the fjords, with the most reliable snow in the park (mid-January to late March). No marked routes: you plan your own.
areas.access: From Route 430; Bakers Brook Hut starts 5 km north of Rocky Harbour (Berry Hill campground road), 8.5 km to the hut.

huts.name: Bakers Brook Hut
huts.by: Gros Morne Cooperating Association with Parks Canada
huts.note: on Bakers Brook Pond, novice-intermediate approach

areas.rules: Gros Morne National Park. Leave a trip plan; carry avalanche gear in the mountains.

links.t: Parks Canada: Gros Morne backcountry skiing
Parks Canada: Gros Morne ski huts

areas.name: Gros Morne: Tablelands and Southwest Gulch
areas.about: Bare orange mantle rock that holds snow in gullies and bowls: Southwest Gulch, The Bowl and Winterhouse Brook. Avalanches happen here.
areas.access: Tablelands trailhead on Route 431 toward Trout River.

huts.name: Southwest Gulch Hut
huts.by: Gros Morne Cooperating Association with Parks Canada

areas.rules: Gros Morne National Park.

links.t: Parks Canada: Gros Morne backcountry skiing
Parks Canada: Gros Morne ski huts

areas.name: Gros Morne: Bonne Bay and Southeast Hills
areas.about: Slopes around Bonne Bay and the Southeast Hills, named by Parks Canada among the park's best snow areas, close to Route 430.
areas.access: Pull-outs along Route 430 near Wiltondale and Rocky Harbour.
areas.rules: Gros Morne National Park.

links.t: Parks Canada: Gros Morne backcountry skiing

areas.name: Blow Me Down Mountains
areas.about: Steep coastal mountains on the Bay of Islands west of Corner Brook, skied from the road to Lark Harbour.
areas.access: Route 450 along the south shore of the Bay of Islands.

areas.name: Torngat Mountains
areas.about: The highest mountains east of the Rockies, at the northern tip of Labrador. Expedition ski touring in polar bear country.
areas.access: Charter flight or boat; guided trips via the park's base camp.
areas.rules: Parks Canada registration and orientation; polar bear safety plan (armed bear guards are strongly advised). No avalanche forecast.

links.t: Parks Canada: Torngat Mountains National Park

areas.name: Mount Carleton
areas.about: The Maritimes' highest peak, in a remote provincial park: winter tours over rolling, forested hills to a bald summit.
areas.access: Mount Carleton Provincial Park, Route 385 north of Plaster Rock (winter access is long).

areas.name: Cape Breton Highlands
areas.about: A windswept plateau with steep valley sides falling to the sea. Snow can be good after big storms; most touring is low-angle on the plateau.
areas.access: Cabot Trail trailheads; check which parts of the Cabot Trail are plowed.
areas.rules: Cape Breton Highlands National Park.

links.t: Parks Canada: Cape Breton Highlands National Park

areas.name: Akshayuk Pass (Auyuittuq)
areas.about: A 97 km ski traverse through a glacier-carved pass on Baffin Island between Pangnirtung and Qikiqtarjuaq, usually 8 to 12 days, with emergency shelters about a day apart.
areas.access: Snowmobile shuttle from Pangnirtung or Qikiqtarjuaq to the park boundary.
areas.rules: Registration and an orientation with Parks Canada are mandatory before you enter and de-register when you leave (arrange it well ahead). Polar bears. No avalanche forecast.
